intro: What actually shipped, not a roadmap. One summary per day in plain language. Older notes may still say Helm; the product is now Trenston.

entries.title: Reset the invite code, cleaner team changes, and a safer first sign-in
entries.description: Team & Access now has a Reset button next to the invite code. Removing someone from a company does not change the code, so a person who left could rejoin with it. Resetting makes the old code stop working right away, and the removal message now reminds you to do it. Creating a company is also safer: pressing Enter twice no longer makes two companies, and a company name is limited to 120 characters, the same as renaming one. If you open a link to a page inside Trenston while signed out, such as a task from an email, you now land on that page after signing in instead of the home page. The sign-in page also says when a sign-in did not finish, and the sign-up page no longer mentions a third-party service by name. Adding and removing people is cleaner too. When a teammate deleted their account, their seat stayed counted, so the owner could be told to upgrade while the plan had room. Seats are now freed when someone is removed, deletes their account, or is deleted from the sign-in provider. Removing a person also clears their department lanes and stored Google connection, so adding them back later starts fresh. Deleting an account clears their roster link, department lanes and the email addresses they had referred, and deleting a company no longer leaves teammates pointing at it. An email address can be invited again after its old account was deleted.

entries.title: Click a month on Financials, a clearer Reports page, and new integration plans
entries.description: On Financials, click a month on the charts, or pick one from the month buttons under Revenue vs expenses, to see exactly what was counted that month. A recurring expense such as a monthly subscription now shows in each month it applies to, with when it started. Two different recurring subscriptions in the same category, for example Cursor Pro and Claude under Software, now both count every month. Before, the newer one replaced the older one. A newer entry with the same name still replaces the old one, so a price change counts once, and the month view tells you when that happens. Reports is now in a clear order with plain names: This week at a glance, CEO Pack, Export for your accountant, Daily report files and Saved reports, with quick links at the top. The last CEO Pack you wrote now stays on the page after a reload. The accountant preview opens only when you ask for it, and saved reports can hold up to six numbers. A month where you made money reads as profit instead of a negative burn. If one file in a batch can't be read, the rest still go through and you can try again on that file. People limited to some finance departments now see only their own figures in the Money check-in. Slack alerts now come with Starter, along with QuickBooks, Xero and Google. SAP Business One moved to Growth and Business, together with HubSpot. Free still includes Google Calendar and Drive. Deleting a workspace or account now cancels its paid subscription first, so you are never billed for a company you removed, and if the cancellation can't be confirmed the delete stops so you can retry. The activity-log export now uses your company's timezone for its date range and no longer lets spreadsheet apps run text as a formula. Saving only the cash balance on Financials can no longer clear your gross margin. Billing is safer too: downgrading now changes your Paddle subscription at the end of the period, so you stop paying the old price, and upgrading while subscribed changes your existing plan instead of starting a second subscription. After a downgrade or cancellation, paid features such as accounting auto-sync, Slack alerts and extra automation rules stop running. Pressing Escape no longer breaks open dialogs, the Excel export keeps typed text as plain text, and quantity and cost fields on Procurement only accept numbers.

entries.title: A money summary on Financials
entries.description: Financials now has a Money summary with three short sections: What's making money, What's losing money and Why this matters. It looks at your last finished month, compares it with the month before, and explains it in plain English. The numbers come straight from your ledger, so the summary always matches the rest of the page. If a month has no revenue or expenses logged, it tells you what to add instead of showing zero. Press Write summary to create it and Refresh to update it. If nothing has changed since the last one, Refresh keeps the saved summary. If AI summaries are unavailable, you'll see a short under maintenance message.

entries.title: A calmer, easier to scan Home page
entries.description: Home now puts the most important things first. The AI summary shows its first two sentences with a Show more link, and the full note is still one click away. What changed lists one line per change with the time on the right, and skips rows that say nothing changed, like a page view with 0 items. What to decide stands out with a priority marker, a clear Review button and long details you can expand. If the AI summary is over a day old, Home tells you so and points you to refresh it. The cash reserve alert no longer suggests a cut in burn that would only add a few days, and points you to raising cash or revenue instead.

entries.title: Runway you can trust mid-month, and a check for money counted twice
entries.description: Runway now uses your last three full months of revenue and expenses. Before, the month in progress was included, so in the middle of a month runway could look longer than it really is. The Financials page, the Model page, the cash reserve alert and the AI now all work from the same numbers, and Financials tells you which months runway is based on. If a month hasn't finished and it's all the history you have, runway is marked as an early estimate. Trenston also warns you when something you typed by hand looks like the same money your accounting system already synced, such as Rent added manually and the rent bill from QuickBooks, Xero or SAP Business One. If your accounting system is connected, your next sync re-reads your records once so every entry follows the latest rules.

entries.title: One Home for everyone, no Gmail access, and clearer access for your team
entries.description: Trenston now has one Home page that fits your role. Owners and executives see the company briefing with their own day underneath, and everyone else sees their own work, notes and updates. The Decisions card no longer appears twice. Telemetry is now called Metrics, and old links still work. Trenston no longer asks for any Gmail access. Connecting Google covers Calendar, the Sheets export and Drive files you pick, and the Privacy and Security pages say so. We checked every page from a team member's point of view and fixed what we found. Money figures now stay with people who have Financials access everywhere, including the AI daily summary, Metrics, the Home headline and revenue retention. Department figures on Home, such as procurement spend, only show for departments you belong to, and HR status on the People page needs HR access. The Executive role now sees everything, including Financials, Financial Modeling, every department and the Company map, but cannot edit the books, HR records, billing or automations. Executives can save their own modeling scenarios. The People / HR role now runs the HR department as its lead, without being added separately. Pages you cannot open now say so right away instead of loading for several seconds, and Billing, Automations and the Company map explain who can open them. The badge next to your name shows your real role, like Executive or Finance, instead of Member for everyone. Teammates no longer see buttons they cannot use, like adding financial entries, setting a cash reserve or assigning departments, and a teammate who hits a plan limit is told to ask the owner to upgrade. Role descriptions in Team & Access now match what each role can do. On the public site, search engines and AI tools can now read the homepage, pricing, testimonials and FAQ without running the app, the copy uses plain words, and the About page has the founder's story.

entries.title: A calmer light mode, a clearer Briefing, and a more reliable calendar and sign-in
entries.description: The app in light mode now has a pure white page, softer card edges, bigger page titles, a warm gold accent for the active page and section labels, and content that stops stretching on very wide screens. The Briefing now puts what needs you first: today's summary, then what changed, what to decide and what to hand off, then your numbers. Duplicate finance tiles moved into a collapsed All metrics section, and the revenue chart loads after the rest of the page so it appears faster. The sidebar is grouped into Today, Money and Company, so the list is shorter and easier to scan, and the Connect your tools card steps aside on shorter screens. The welcome card now appears once, on the first page you open, instead of on every page. Dates read like Oct 14, 2026 across Tasks, Briefing, Procurement, HR, Legal and Calendar, and empty pages take up less space. Calendar events now appear at the time you typed. Before, an 11:00 AM event could show at 7 PM in Manila, and it could also reach Google Calendar at the wrong hour. Both are fixed. Signing in is more reliable: slow sign-in provider responses are no longer abandoned early, the connection starts sooner, and the error only appears after a much longer wait. Deleting a user in the sign-in provider now also ends their Trenston session. Phones got bigger tap areas for small controls, and every button and link shows a clear ring when you move through the page with the keyboard, with a skip to main content link on every page. On the public site, the homepage picture loads faster, the integrations section is a slim moving strip of logos and names, a Start free button now follows How it works, and the QuickBooks line says it is approved by Intuit and only reads your data. We also count button clicks and sign-up views anonymously, with no cookies and no user IDs, so we can see where visitors drop off. Behind the scenes, Tasks and Integrations keep what you were looking at if a refresh fails, task moves are queued so quick drags do not collide, and Gmail updates stop after you disconnect. The website now builds with Vite instead of Create React App, and the server software and database drivers were upgraded.

entries.title: Learn as you go, Automations, Company map and quick add
entries.description: Trenston now teaches itself inside the app. Each main page shows a short welcome card the first time you open it, with a Show me around button that dims the screen and points at the real buttons one at a time. A new ? button at the top of every page explains that page in plain words and can replay its tour. The Get started list now has a Show me button on each step that opens the right page and highlights exactly what to press, and teammates get their own list instead of the owner's. Money and sales terms like runway, burn, MRR and pipeline have a small (i) that explains them, and empty pages now give an example of what to add. A new Automations page lets the workspace owner set rules once: when a work order is overdue, a supplier delay blocks production, a legal deadline is near, a deal stalls, or cash runway gets short, Trenston creates a task for the right person or shows an alert. Ready-made rules get you started in one click. Each thing fires once, and a rule can create at most 10 tasks per run, so turning one on never floods the board. Trenston also checks the finance ledger once a day for entries that look duplicated, one-off expenses far above the usual, and revenue that drops or stops, and shows each finding with a plain explanation. None of this uses AI, so it costs nothing to run. Signing in is also faster: sessions are verified without a round trip to the sign-in provider, the sign-in screen starts instantly on repeat visits, and the error screen now offers Try again instead of forcing a sign-out. Assistant connections like Claude now last 30 days before they ask you to sign in again. A new Company map page (owner only) draws your company from records you already have: cash and runway in the middle, where money comes from on the left, where it goes on the right, what you have promised underneath, your team on top for workspaces with more than one person, and anything going wrong in red with a plain next step. It only shows what your records say, and asks for the missing facts instead of guessing when there is too little data. The search bar (Ctrl+K or Cmd+K) now doubles as quick add: type task, decision or note followed by what you mean, for example "task call the supplier friday for Ann", and it shows exactly what it understood, including the date, person and priority, and saves only when you press Enter. If a name matches two people it asks which one. Automations now have per-plan rule limits: 2 on Free, 5 on Starter, 15 on Growth and 25 on Business. None of this uses AI, so it costs nothing to run. The app now looks like the website: the same type throughout, headings set like the site's, rounder buttons and cards, and black primary buttons in the light theme. On the website, the home page opens on a white hero, the header logo is larger, and buttons have rounded corners. Every page, on the website and in the app, now uses one professional typeface, Inter, with its tighter Display style for big headlines and evenly spaced figures so money lines up in columns. Emails use it too where the email app allows. Key headline words on the website now sit on a tilted navy tag with a yellow frame behind it. On phones, the app now has a bottom bar for the pages you use most, with More for everything else. Text boxes no longer make iPhones zoom in, pop-up forms always fit the screen and scroll, small buttons are easier to tap, and the site and app respect the iPhone notch and home bar. The search bar is smarter: it now finds your own tasks, decisions, deals and people by name, forgives a typo, matches words in any order, ranks the best match first, and offers to ask Trenston when nothing matches. Pressing Enter right after typing always acts on what you see, and typing just task, decision or note takes you to that page instead of starting an entry. Quick add also understands dates like 12/10, on the 5th, next month and next quarter, shows the year when a date falls in next year, no longer reads a quantity after May as a date, and treats urgent: as high priority.

entries.title: Tighter privacy for financial activity and AI connections
entries.description: Activity entries from Financials, which can include amounts such as logged revenue, now only show in the Briefing and the activity feed for people with Financials access, matching the Financials page itself. Removing someone from a workspace now ends all of their API keys and AI assistant connections for good, so re-inviting them never brings old access back. Deleting a workspace or an account also deletes its API keys and connections. The consent screen for connecting an assistant marks Claude's own sign-in as verified and labels any other app as unverified. The Help page has a new step-by-step guide to connecting an AI assistant, and the Security page explains exactly what read-only access allows.

entries.title: API keys, and connecting Claude and other AI assistants
entries.description: Growth and Business workspaces can now create personal API keys in Settings, under API keys. A key lets a script or an AI assistant read your briefing, decisions, tasks, your assigned work across departments, and, if you have Financials access, a financial summary. Keys are read-only: they cannot change anything. Each key sees exactly what its owner can see in Trenston, only in that workspace, so department and Financials access rules still apply. Keys are shown once, stored only as a one-way hash, limited to 60 requests a minute, and can be revoked at any time. Removing someone from the workspace stops their keys immediately. For AI assistants that support the Model Context Protocol, the Trenston MCP server exposes the same read-only data as tools. Missing figures come back marked as not entered, never as zero. You can also connect Claude without a key: add the Trenston connector in Claude, sign in to Trenston, and approve read-only access on the consent screen. Connected assistants appear in Settings under Connected apps, where you can disconnect them at any time.

entries.title: Try a demo before setup, one account menu, and a page on how Trenston compares
entries.description: New owners now see a welcome screen with two choices: explore a demo company with sample data, or go straight to setting up their own. While you browse the demo a banner stays on screen, and Set up my company clears the sample data and takes you to setup. The sidebar and header are simpler: one account menu in the top right holds Billing, Integrations, Help and Log out, and Settings sits at the bottom of the sidebar. Integrations is still on the Settings page too. On Telemetry, the MRR and ARR Add data prompt no longer runs into its link. Disconnecting an integration now asks you to confirm first, team and invite errors say what went wrong in plain language, dark mode text is easier to read on status labels, and your plan is no longer shown twice in the header. The browser tab always shows the Trenston icon, now with rounded corners so Safari does not draw an outline around it, and the home page and app tab titles read simply Trenston. A new page, How Trenston compares, explains where Trenston fits next to spreadsheets, dashboards, enterprise suites and chat tools, what it is not, and when another tool is the better choice.

entries.title: Faster public pages, updates that no longer break open tabs, and a working Invite a CEO
entries.description: Public pages now download about 27% less JavaScript (288 KB down to 209 KB compressed). The signed-in app and the sign-in code load only after you sign in, so the homepage, pricing and features open sooner. If you have Trenston open when we ship an update, the next page you open reloads once to the new version instead of showing an error that Try again could not fix; if that cannot work, the screen says Trenston was just updated and offers Reload, or says you are offline. Error messages are plain language: a dropped connection, a timeout, an expired session or a busy server each say what happened, never raw technical text. Invite a CEO in Settings no longer fails for owners who did not have a referral link yet. Joining with an invite code no longer hangs on Joining, and a lost connection is no longer reported as a bad code. Telemetry, HR Employees, HR Offboarding and coming-soon departments now link to the next step instead of only describing it. New companies default to USD on the setup screen, matching the rest of the product. Telemetry no longer scrolls sideways on phones, and the same fix covers 21 layouts across the app. Settings offers Light, Dark and Auto, matching the sidebar. The cookie notice no longer covers the last button on setup pages, the sidebar fades when more departments sit below the fold, Revenue vs Expenses on Financials has a legend, and dismissing the Connect your tools card now stays dismissed.

entries.title: My Day, Tasks and Telemetry fixes, and fresher search listings
entries.description: My Day no longer goes blank when a background refresh fails, and each section now loads and shows its own errors, so one slow feed cannot take the page down. HR leave requests, yours and the ones you approve as a lead, now appear in My Work, sample tasks assigned to You show up, and today on calendar meetings follows your workspace timezone. Tasks rejects unknown board columns, only lets you drag tasks that are yours or that you can assign, and marks overdue tasks using your workspace date. On Telemetry, the activity heatmap anchors its weeks and its future cutoff to your workspace date instead of UTC, suggested risks you already added no longer reappear, reaching the 20-risk limit now says so, and the target growth field is limited to between -100% and 1,000%. For search engines, the sitemap now regenerates on every build with a current date, public pages carry richer text and FAQ data without JavaScript, and app and sign-in pages are kept out of search results so they do not compete with marketing pages. Privacy now explains how Google data is used under Google's Limited Use rules.

entries.title: Complete data export and deletion, AI disclosures, and a steadier Briefing and Decision Center
entries.description: Exporting or deleting your workspace data now covers nine workspace collections that were missed before, with a test that fails if a new one is forgotten. Security and Privacy now name the AI services involved (Anthropic and Google Cloud Document AI), add a Your data, your exit section, and soften the zero-retention wording to match provider backups. Security, Privacy, Terms and Refunds now show their full text without JavaScript. Briefing uses your workspace timezone for the weekday header, so a Manila-time workspace no longer shows the wrong day, and it no longer invents 0% month-over-month changes for Burn and Runway. A failed background refresh now shows one notice instead of repeating, Gmail draft buttons disable while one request is running, Briefing updates after maintenance ticket changes, and its headline numbers use the same monospace figures as Financials. Decision Center no longer goes blank when a background refresh fails, decisions delegated to others stay actionable instead of showing as resolved, lists rank High, then Medium, then Low, approving or dismissing a suggestion can no longer be applied twice, and the calendar updates when decisions change.

entries.title: Financial Modeling, runway warnings, and a calmer setup
entries.description: A new Financial Modeling page (Growth and Business) starts from your last three months of real revenue and expenses. Move sliders for revenue growth and expense growth, add planned hires and one-time events like a funding round, and runway, the month cash runs out, break-even and ending cash update instantly. Save scenarios and compare up to three on one chart against your current trajectory. On every plan, you can now set a minimum cash reserve in Financials, and Trenston warns you before cash is projected to fall below it, with the date and what a 10% cut in burn would change. It also flags burn rising two months in a row, revenue falling below its recent average, a drop in completed tasks, and open pipeline that will not cover your sales targets. Open any warning to see exactly how it was worked out. Financial warnings only reach people with Financials access, in the app, by email and in Slack, and the weekly pack email now only goes to people who can see Financials. Setup is calmer too: company details are one plain form instead of a four-step wizard, and the departments and starting-point steps are simple lists. Every browser pop-up (new company, deletes, removals) is now an in-app dialog, integrations show their real logos, and the founder note is written in the founder's own voice.

entries.title: Every screen links to the record behind it, plus trust fixes
entries.description: Briefing, My Day, Decisions, the calendar, and department pages now deep-link straight to the exact decision, task, deal, ledger row, or department item they reference, scrolled to and briefly highlighted, instead of dropping you on a generic page. Approving a decision offers to create a follow-up task; winning a deal shows exactly where the revenue landed in Financials with a link to it; a teammate's blocker can become a decision in one click. Fixed real bugs along the way: the daily briefing email's button led to a dead page, editing an AI-drafted decision silently wiped its confidence score, Ask Trenston could lose your latest conversation or spin forever on an empty reply, switching browser tabs mid-edit could wipe unsaved changes on department pages, won-deal revenue could book to the wrong month or stick around after a deal was un-won or deleted, all-day deadlines showed across two calendar days in Manila, and the setup checklist un-ticked itself every morning so solo founders could never finish it. Trenston now also speaks to founders first, CEOs second, everywhere from the homepage to in-app permission messages.

entries.title: Sturdier integrations, home currency and timezone, Ask memory
entries.description: QuickBooks, Xero, and SAP Business One keep syncing through temporary blips instead of disconnecting you, pick up voids and deletions, and roll totals in your workspace home currency as net amounts (tax and foreign currency handled consistently, no hardcoded dollar signs). Google Calendar and Gmail are one Google Workspace connection: events follow your workspace timezone, and Gmail drafts land with cleaner headers. Slack webhooks are stored more safely, and integration errors show plain customer-safe messages. Clearing sample data no longer risks wiping real records. Ask Trenston keeps conversation memory across turns and distinguishes errors from interruptions. Leftover Helm labels in settings and integrations now say Trenston. In the same ship window: Briefing keeps what you already see when a background refetch fails and respects finance loading and access; homepage marketing copy dropped em dashes for plain commas; and billing and plan language says users instead of seats.

entries.title: Briefing polish, light-mode surfaces, and a quieter sidebar
entries.description: Briefing charts no longer label every y-axis tick as $0k. Small ranges now show real dollars, and the current-period bars use brand gold in both themes. Empty finance KPIs and “Not tracked” department cards became actionable add prompts instead of underlined fake links; status dots follow one healthy / attention / alert / empty system with a short legend. Light mode keeps a pure white page canvas while cards sit on a barely-off-white lift so panels separate without cream; Active stays only on the top-bar pill, nav digit shortcuts read as hover hints, and the selected sidebar item uses a soft gold tint instead of a solid white pill. Also shipped the vertical cir-tabs sidebar rail, CirNote toasts for Gmail AI drafts, and clearer delete / danger-confirm patterns across the app.

entries.title: Cockpit redesign, themes, department APIs, and solo founders
entries.description: The signed-in app got a full command-surface pass: sidebar Ask Trenston CTA and upgrade/connect promo, desktop top bar with search and plan badge, a Briefing cockpit hero (metric switcher, period chart, Assistant / Spending / Decisions), and a two-column Ask Trenston layout with a context rail. Light remaps are scoped so dark mode works again; Briefing charts, gold spend meters, and KPIs stay readable on dark backgrounds. Marketing moved to navy home / cream auth with an Outway-style footer, ember accent, and transparent favicons, plus Tansher Dhawan, Founder in the footer with LinkedIn. Sales order-book, maintenance ops, and procurement settings APIs are wired and tested. Company setup now asks whether you have people you can delegate to: solo workspaces get Flag for later instead of handoffs, and Onboarding drops Invite your finance team. Also fixed People remove after revoke, error toasts blanking Maintenance/Order book, QuickBooks OAuth mislabeled as Google, ⌘K missing pages, and a broader audit on rate limits, sync, and billing.

entries.title: Helm Control is Trenston, plus public pricing and personal Google
entries.description: The product formerly called Helm Control is now Trenston at trenston.com: same cockpit, new name and domain; helmcontrol.online bookmarks redirect here. Department pages keep recently loaded data when you switch tabs so Briefing, Financials, HR, and Production don’t skeleton-reload every visit. Each teammate connects their own Google Calendar and Gmail (not a shared workspace mailbox). Standalone /pricing publishes Free, Starter, Growth, and Business with structured data and llms.txt, and a public /integrations page lists what each connection actually does today (Google, QuickBooks, Xero, SAP Business One, HubSpot, Slack).

entries.title: SAP B1, honest financials, and tighter Ask / Decision Center
entries.description: Financials can pull A/R and A/P from SAP Business One Service Layer into the same pipeline as QuickBooks and Xero. Burn, MRR, and runway distinguish “not entered” from a confirmed zero; future-dated ledger rows no longer inflate current metrics. Decision Center ranks pending items by impact within severity, and a single failed AI draft no longer clears the board. Ask Trenston and department context respect membership and finance:write, so nothing leaks across lanes. AI summaries label when underlying department data may be stale.

entries.title: Document library, alert emails, leave cancel, and billing clarity
entries.description: Bills, receipts, and legal files sit in private Cloudflare R2 with signed downloads and tighter legal access. Render cron jobs send high-severity daily alerts and the weekly leadership pack email, separate from in-app Briefing. Employees can cancel their own pending leave without waiting on HR. After Paddle checkout, plan state refreshes cleanly, seat and AI-extract over-limit usage is obvious, and leftover Stripe UI is gone.

entries.title: Public changelog and ⌘K search across the product
entries.description: We added this public /changelog: hand-written ship notes in plain language (not a roadmap, not auto-generated from git), linked from the marketing footer, SEO, and sitemap so buyers can see what actually landed. Inside the signed-in app, ⌘K quick search reaches settings sections and public marketing pages without leaving the cockpit.
